summary: Kootenai National Forest 40-foot pole tower with an 8-by-8-foot cab, built 1934 and destroyed 1958; no source consulted describes the site today.

facts.design: 40-foot pole tower with an 8-by-8-foot cab; a log cabin is listed with it
facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1958; no source consulted describes what remains at the site.
facts.location: about 12 miles north-northeast of Yaak, Lincoln County, Montana; about three-quarters of a mile south of Wood Mountain

events.note: 1934: 40-foot pole tower with an 8-by-8-foot cab, log cabin listed with it

evidence.supports: Kootenai National Forest, Lincoln County, Montana
built 1934, 40-foot pole tower with 8-by-8-foot cab and log cabin
evidence.quote: 1934: 40' pole tower with 8x8' cab, log cabin.

evidence.supports: about three-quarters of a mile south of Wood Mountain
a separate Lincoln County list places it in the same forest

sources.title: Montana Lookouts, Forest Fire Lookout Association

notes_for_editor: Built and destroyed dates and dimensions come only from firelookout.com. The Lincoln County list gives a township-range-section code, 37N-30W-18, which was not converted to a place. The 40-foot figure is the tower height as the guide words it ("40' pole tower"); the page does not give total height, so the story attributes it to firelookout.com and does not state it as an overall height. Web searches found no other source for Grubstake or Wood Mountain. Name collision: a Crystal Mountain (Washington) page mentions a Grubstake Point on a ski map and says a lookout there likely never existed. That is a different site and was not used. Record coordinates match the FFLA list exactly.
